title: Hanuman Mandir, Prayagraj - The Sacred Bade Hanuman Ji Temple Near Sangam
content:
Hanuman Mandir, Prayagraj

Hanuman Mandir in Prayagraj, popularly known as Bade Hanuman Ji Mandir, is one of the most revered and spiritually powerful temples in North India. Located close to the holy Triveni Sangam, this ancient temple is famous for its unique reclining (letiye hue) idol of Lord Hanuman, which makes it distinct from other Hanuman temples across India. Every year, thousands of devotees visit this sacred place to seek strength, protection, and blessings.

Historical Background and Legends

According to religious beliefs, the idol of Bade Hanuman Ji is Swayambhu (self-manifested) and dates back to ancient times. Local legends associate the temple with the Ramayana period, suggesting that Lord Hanuman himself chose this place to reside after the completion of Lord Rama’s mission on earth. Over centuries, kings, saints, and common devotees have contributed to the temple’s upkeep, strengthening its importance as a spiritual center in Prayagraj.

Unique Reclining Idol of Lord Hanuman

The most remarkable feature of this temple is the giant reclining statue of Lord Hanuman, a rare depiction in Hindu temples. The idol rests in a calm, sleeping posture, symbolizing peace and eternal devotion to Lord Rama.

One of the most fascinating aspects is that during monsoon seasons and Kumbh Mela, the water level of the Ganga rises, and the idol becomes partially submerged. Devotees consider this phenomenon extremely auspicious and believe that it brings prosperity and protection to the city.

Religious Significance and Beliefs

Hanuman Mandir is believed to act as a protector of Prayagraj. Many devotees believe that as long as Bade Hanuman Ji rests peacefully, the city remains safe from major disasters. People visit the temple to pray for:

  • Physical and mental strength
  • Protection from negative energies
  • Success in work and education
  • Good health and family well-being

Tuesdays and Saturdays are especially significant, with large crowds gathering for darshan and special prayers.

Temple Architecture and Complex

While the temple architecture is simple, it holds deep spiritual value. The underground sanctum where the idol rests creates a unique devotional atmosphere. The temple complex also includes:

  • Smaller shrines of Lord Rama and other deities
  • Prayer halls for devotees
  • Shops selling flowers, sindoor, and prasad

Its proximity to important sacred sites makes it a key stop on the Prayagraj pilgrimage circuit.

Nearby Sacred Attractions

The temple is surrounded by several major religious landmarks:

  • Triveni Sangam - The confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati
  • Allahabad Fort - A Mughal-era fort built by Akbar. 
  • Akshaya Vat - The immortal banyan tree
  • Saraswati Koop - An ancient sacred well

These sites together enhance the spiritual experience of visitors.

Festivals and Special Occasions

The temple comes alive during major Hindu festivals such as:

  • Hanuman Jayanti
  • Ram Navami
  • Kumbh Mela and Magh Mela

During these times, the temple is beautifully decorated, and special aartis and bhajans are performed, creating a deeply devotional environment.

Visitor Information

  • Location: Near Triveni Sangam, Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh
  • Temple Timings: Early morning to late evening
  • Best time to visit: Morning hours or evening aarti
  • Entry fee: Free
  • Dress code: Modest attire recommended
